decisions.reason: The approved bullet appearance does not change Tab-driven level transitions, hierarchy structure, or nested alignment behavior.
The source concerns bullet-list visual appearance and does not change numbered or multilevel list alignment.
Applying a customer-provided bullet design does not change the PBU naming prefix, naming language, or covered style categories.
Bullet-list appearance is independent of keeping pasted content within column and page boundaries.
The source specifies bullet appearance but does not modify legacy copy-paste stability, source files, migration targets, or robustness standards.
The approved bullet design does not affect manual line-break entry after pasted content.
The style system already requires consistent application across all templates; the bullet-specific appearance decision does not change that requirement's specification reference or coverage.
Bullet-list visual design does not change table layout stability, right-column boundaries, or the existing table-adjustment ambiguity.
The bullet appearance decision does not alter the supported Microsoft Word environment or the general operational-reliability constraint.
